observations: Photo 0 shows a metal transmission/gearbox housing, likely an automatic transmission bell-housing with a visible blue torque converter.
Bolt pattern and electrical connector (green wire visible) are seen on the casing.
No legible part number, casting number, or Toyota logo is visible anywhere on the housing.
A watermark reading something like 'SPARE PARTS' overlays the image; this is not an identifying mark from the manufacturer.
Background shows other disassembled engine/transmission parts, consistent with a used-parts yard.

claims.evidence: No casting number, part number, or Toyota marking visible in photo 0 to confirm vehicle fitment.
No origin stamp, tag, or paperwork shown in photo 0.
Electrical connector is partly visible in photo 0 but pin count cannot be counted from the image.
No model-year-specific marking or documentation visible.
No functional test, video, or fluid condition shown; subjective claim with no supporting evidence.

risks.risk: Wrong vehicle/engine fitment (could be for a different Camry generation or trim, or not a Camry at all)
risks.proof: Clear close-up photo of the casting/part number stamped on the housing, matched against a Toyota parts catalog.
risks.if_unproven: priced as unverified-fitment, generic used automatic transmission

risks.risk: Internal mechanical failure (slipping, worn clutch packs, damaged torque converter) not visible from outside
risks.proof: Video of the transmission being bench-tested or installed and shifting through gears, plus fluid condition check.
Photo of drained fluid color/smell description, or photo of dipstick/fluid port.
risks.if_unproven: priced as having unknown fluid condition, treat as needing full service

risks.risk: Hidden cracks or damage on the housing not shown in a single angle photo
risks.proof: Multiple photos from all sides including the mating surface and torque converter bolts.
risks.if_unproven: priced as having possible undisclosed external damage

risks.risk: Mileage/usage history unknown (could be high-mileage take-out part)
risks.proof: Photo of donor vehicle odometer or any paperwork/tag indicating mileage.

proof_requests: Close-up photo of the casting number / part number stamped on the transmission case.
Video of the gearbox being tested (e.g., spinning the input shaft, torque converter movement, or installed and shifting).
Photo of the transmission fluid (color, smell description) from the dipstick or drain plug.
Additional photos from other angles (top, side opposite to the one shown, mating surface) to check for cracks or damage.
Any documentation or tag indicating the donor vehicle's mileage and country of origin.
response.reason: This is clearly a used automatic transmission/gearbox unit, but no marking in the photo confirms it is specifically a Toyota Camry unit or its exact fitment years, and there is no evidence of function, so it must be priced at the worst case as an unverified-fitment, untested used gearbox.
